# Key numbers (generated by `python src/make_viva_pack.py`; do not edit by hand)

Every number below was computed by re-fitting the models in this run.

## A. Linear regression (target: expected_score, not ground truth)

* n_train = 360 pairs (24 requirements), n_test = 90 pairs (6 requirements), p = 7
  columns (intercept + 6 features).
* Condition number of X_train = 114.45; rank = 7.
* Solvers agree: |β̂_inverse − β̂_lstsq| ≤ 7.46e-14,
  |β̂_sklearn − β̂_lstsq| ≤ 2.13e-14.

| feature | β̂ | SE | t = β̂/SE |
|---|---|---|---|
| intercept | 0.2962 | 2.3888 | 0.12 |
| distance_km | -0.1568 | 0.0758 | -2.07 |
| within_radius | 18.1357 | 2.2583 | 8.03 |
| category_match | 59.4411 | 1.6868 | 35.24 |
| keyword_in_title | 15.4676 | 4.9057 | 3.15 |
| n_categories | -3.2396 | 0.6550 | -4.95 |
| is_chain | 3.4746 | 4.0048 | 0.87 |

SE = √diag(s²(XᵀX)⁻¹) (valid only if the Gaussian, constant-variance assumptions hold).

| quantity | train | test |
|---|---|---|
| RSS = Σ(y − ŷ)² | 80739.8798 | 27430.0652 |
| MSE = RSS/n | 224.2774 | 304.7785 |
| RMSE = √MSE | 14.9759 | 17.4579 |
| MAE = mean abs(y − ŷ) | 11.3600 | 13.9775 |
| R² = 1 − RSS/TSS | 0.7983 | 0.7510 |

* TSS_train = Σ(y − ȳ)² = 400293.6000, so R²_train = 1 − 80739.8798/400293.6000 = 0.7983.
* σ̂²_MLE = RSS/n = 80739.8798/360 = 224.2774;  σ̂_MLE = 14.9759.
* s² = RSS/(n−p) = 80739.8798/353 = 228.7249;  s = 15.1237.
* Bias factor (n−p)/n = 353/360 = 0.980556; σ̂²_MLE / s² = 0.980556 (identical, as theory says).
* Maximised log-likelihood, plugged in:
  ℓ = −(n/2)·ln(2πσ̂²) − RSS/(2σ̂²) = -1305.1370 + (-180.0000) = -1485.1370
  (the second term is always −n/2 = -180.0 at σ̂²_MLE).
  Closed form −(n/2)(ln(2πσ̂²) + 1) = -1485.1370; direct Σ log φ(eᵢ; 0, σ̂) = -1485.1370.
* Train MSE = σ̂²_MLE: True (same number, different meaning).
* Residual diagnostics (train): skew -0.311, excess kurtosis
  2.220, Shapiro-Wilk p = 3.59e-08;
  fitted values below 0: 61 train, 14 test.
* AI judge consistency on 45 pairs: blind r = 0.9762, MAD = 4.133
  (non-blind r = 0.9957, MAD = 3.000).

## B. Logistic regression (target: is_pharmacy weak labels)

* Split: train 3689 vendors (389 pharmacies), test 923
  (97 pharmacies, prevalence 0.1051).
* Full design: 442 columns, rank 442.
  Single-feature separators: 276. Joint LP optimum 6017
  (> 0 means separated, so the MLE does not exist).
* Log-likelihoods on train: null (intercept only) -1242.7964; full unpenalised IRLS
  -103.5582 (not a maximum, it keeps creeping up); small-model MLE
  -857.2226; L2 model -146.0539.
* Full model: IRLS ‖β‖ after 100 iterations = 650.76;
  IRLS vs sklearn coefficients differ by up to
  2705.12
  despite the same ℓ.
* Small model: tokens ['shop', 'store', 'and', 'sri', 'chennai', 'stores', 'pharmacy', 's', 'home', 'centre']; IRLS converged in 8 iterations;
  |β̂_IRLS − β̂_sklearn| ≤ 1.78e-15.
* L2 model: C = 10 (λ = 0.1), chosen by 5-fold CV on train.

| model | TN | FP | FN | TP | accuracy | precision | recall | F1 | ROC-AUC | PR-AUC |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| L2 (MAP, not MLE) | 825 | 1 | 11 | 86 | 0.9870 | 0.9885 | 0.8866 | 0.9348 | 0.9842 | 0.9465 |
| Small-model MLE | 826 | 0 | 62 | 35 | 0.9328 | 1.0000 | 0.3608 | 0.5303 | 0.7438 | 0.4695 |
| Full unpenalised (invalid MLE) | 816 | 10 | 12 | 85 | 0.9762 | 0.8947 | 0.8763 | 0.8854 | 0.9762 | 0.9094 |

Majority baseline (always predict 0): accuracy 0.8949, recall 0, ROC-AUC 0.5,
PR-AUC = prevalence 0.1051.

## C. Why not linear regression for the 0/1 target (linear probability model)

Fitting OLS to is_pharmacy with the same 442 columns gives test predictions
from -0.311 to 1.802: 326 below 0 and 18 above 1 out of 923,
which are impossible as probabilities. The logistic model's σ(Xβ̂) is always inside (0, 1).

## D. Extended Unit-II models (`python src/extended_models.py`)

Same data, splits and seed as above; every hyperparameter chosen by CV on the training split.

### D1. Regression (target: expected_score, not ground truth)

| model | train R² | test R² | test RMSE | test MAE |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| OLS (Gaussian MLE) | 0.7983 | 0.7510 | 17.4579 | 13.9775 |
| Ridge (L2, MAP) | 0.7983 | 0.7510 | 17.4579 | 13.9775 |
| Robust (Huber) | 0.7955 | 0.7630 | 17.0318 | 13.7805 |
| Bayesian linear | 0.7983 | 0.7510 | 17.4578 | 13.9639 |
| Kernel ridge (poly deg 2) | 0.8664 | 0.8082 | 15.3205 | 11.7256 |
| Kernel ridge (RBF) | 0.8731 | 0.8127 | 15.1413 | 11.4336 |

* **Ridge**: grouped 4-fold CV chose λ = 0.001, the smallest value on the grid,
  so ridge ≈ OLS. With 6 well-conditioned features there is nothing to shrink.
* **Huber** (ε = 1.35): 121 of 360 training pairs
  have |residual| > ε·scale (scale = 9.2588) and get linear instead of squared loss.
  Intercept -0.8642 (OLS 0.2962).
* **Bayesian linear regression** (evidence maximisation): noise precision α =
  0.004385 (noise variance 1/α = 228.0577),
  weight precision λ = 0.001456 (a weak prior, so the posterior
  mean ≈ OLS). The closed-form posterior matches sklearn to 2.27e-13.
  Posterior sd of β: category_match 1.6803, within_radius 2.2464.
  Test: mean predictive sd 15.2786; 95% interval coverage
  0.9333.
* **Kernel ridge**: polynomial degree 2 (α = 3.162) and RBF (α = 0.1,
  γ = 0.03162); the kernels add feature interactions that the linear model cannot.

### D2. Classification (target: weak is_pharmacy labels, test set)

| model | tn | fp | fn | tp | accuracy | precision | recall | f1 | roc_auc | pr_auc |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Logistic L2 (MAP), Phase 1 | 825 | 1 | 11 | 86 | 0.9870 | 0.9885 | 0.8866 | 0.9348 | 0.9842 | 0.9465 |
| Logistic small-model MLE, Phase 1 | 826 | 0 | 62 | 35 | 0.9328 | 1.0000 | 0.3608 | 0.5303 | 0.7438 | 0.4695 |
| Fisher LDA (discriminant) | 823 | 3 | 62 | 35 | 0.9296 | 0.9211 | 0.3608 | 0.5185 | 0.8786 | 0.6055 |
| Bernoulli naive Bayes (generative) | 820 | 6 | 11 | 86 | 0.9816 | 0.9348 | 0.8866 | 0.9101 | 0.9785 | 0.9365 |
| Bayesian logistic (Laplace) | 825 | 1 | 11 | 86 | 0.9870 | 0.9885 | 0.8866 | 0.9348 | 0.9539 | 0.9196 |
| SVM linear | 825 | 1 | 11 | 86 | 0.9870 | 0.9885 | 0.8866 | 0.9348 | 0.9805 | 0.9407 |
| SVM RBF kernel | 819 | 7 | 13 | 84 | 0.9783 | 0.9231 | 0.8660 | 0.8936 | 0.9707 | 0.9183 |

* **Fisher LDA**: shared-covariance Gaussian classes, auto (Ledoit-Wolf) shrinkage.
* **Bernoulli naive Bayes**: Laplace smoothing α = 1.0.
* **Bayesian logistic (Laplace)**: prior λ = 0.1; MAP by penalised IRLS
  (converged True); posterior ≈ N(β_MAP, (XᵀWX + λP)⁻¹); probit-approximated
  predictive. Test log loss: plug-in 0.0583, predictive
  0.1065; mean |shift| 0.0545,
  max 0.2076.
* **SVM**: linear C = 1 with 342 support vectors; RBF C =
  10 with 1155 support vectors (of 3689 training vendors).
